subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: traffic quarantine + mirror window proposal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: traffic quarantine + mirror window proposal

Maya — following our run-through last week, attached is a concise proposal for the mirror window and the traffic quarantine that Pioneer wants during the Hosted→Dedicated swap. Goal: validate sizing under production-like traffic, exercise KV cache priming, and have a short quarantine to protect tail latency while we ramp.

Key asks (short):
- Reserve the staging & canary slots for 11/30–12/02 (see proposed windows in the Drive).
- We’ll run a 4-hour mirror (read/write proxy) + 2 small canaries (5% and 25%) before full cutover.
- Redwood to provision the following sizing baseline for the trial: 8 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized variants) for model-v1, plus 2 warm spares.
- Pioneer to provide a 24h sample traffic CSV (attached) and confirmation of peak RPS and acceptable error budgets.

Pass criteria for the mirror:
- 99th percentile token latency < 400ms for default completion traffic mix.
- No more than 2% increase in error rate vs. hosted baseline.
- Successful KV cache warm-up demonstrating at least 30% token-cost reduction in steady state.

I’ve attached a draft SLA for the migration (pioneer-sla-draft.pdf) and the traffic sample you shared earlier (traffic-pattern-sample.csv). Can Karthik and Ben confirm the resource sizing and the priming plan by EOD? Monica, looping you for post-cutover monitoring cadence and rollback owner.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Pioneer HealthTech Procurement <procurement@pioneerhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: traffic quarantine + mirror window proposal

Camila — thanks, this is helpful and the timelines look sensible. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can provide a 48h traffic dump (production) by tomorrow morning. Peak sustained RPS during business hours is ~1,200 requests/min (burst to 2,000 briefly). Typical completion length is 80–120 tokens.
- Our risk tolerance for the quarantine: we want the quarantine actively enforced for the first 6 hours post-switchover; during that window we expect an explicit rollback threshold of any latency regression >20% at p95.
- We will need a single-day procurement sign-off to meet the 11/30 start; procurement copied for visibility.

Action for Redwood: please confirm the canary lanes and whether the proposed GPU mix (8 + 2 spares) handles a 2x traffic burst without dropping below the 99th latency target. Also confirm whether the canary will be routed through the same cache layer or run a cold path.

— Maya
Director, Platform Engineering
Pioneer HealthTech
maya.gupta@pioneerhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: traffic quarantine + mirror window proposal

Maya — quick sizing note from infra: the proposed fleet (8 A100-equivalent + 2 warm spares) should cover your steady state and short bursts up to ~2x if we enable the following:
- Use the quantized FP16 path we validated earlier (saves ~35% memory and kernel time).
- Configure a conservative batch ceiling (max batch tokens = 512) and a throttle curve that limits concurrency during the first 6h quarantine.
- Enable KV cache priming using a 30-minute pre-warm that replays recent hot prefixes (we’ll coordinate keys).

Expected outcomes in the mirror run (approx):
- Baseline steady RPS target: 20 rps (80–120 token avg) -> ~1.6k tokens/sec per GPU aggregate; we’ll monitor token-level throughput in the Console.
- Canary lanes: we’ll open lane A at 5% of production writes (live mirror) for 1 hour, then lane B at 25% for 2 hours. If p95 latency or error spikes exceed thresholds at any step, we’ll throttle back to previous step and investigate.

Ben — can you own the canary script and the traffic-shaping rules? Monica — please lead monitoring playbook & on-call for the 11/30 window. I’ll drop a short runbook into the Drive tonight.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Pioneer HealthTech Procurement <procurement@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: traffic quarantine + mirror window proposal

Thanks all — summary and next steps so we have an actionable checklist: 
1) Redwood confirms resource reservation for 11/30 02:00–10:00 PST for mirror + canaries (Karthik) — CONFIRMED: 8 GPUs + 2 spares reserved.
2) Pioneer to provide 48h traffic dump by 11/25 10:00 PST (Maya / Procurement).
3) Pre-warm/priming: Redwood will run a 30-minute KV cache priming immediately before the mirror window (Karthik/Ben).
4) Canary sequence: 5% (1h) -> 25% (2h) -> evaluate -> progressive ramp. Rollback threshold = p95 > baseline *1.2 or error rate +2%.
5) Monitoring: Monica to run live dashboard and own rollback trigger; contact list included in the Drive runbook.
6) Post-mirror acceptance: joint sign-off via HubSpot record within 6 hours after mirror; if accepted we schedule a 24h blackout then full cutover.

Ben/Monica/Karthik — please add the canary automation links and the exact runbook steps to the Drive doc by EOD so Procurement can sign off. Maya — if the procurement team can confirm the single-day approval path, we’ll lock 11/30.

Onwards — Camila
